text: Is having a skin tone or color preference weird or basically racist? Guys, are you actually trying to get me cancelled with this type of questions or what? Hi sir, I'm here to ask you about a sensitive topic that I have come across. It's been bothering me and I would like to hear your opinion on it. I'm sorry if it's troublesome, I just look up to you and I'm kind of a fan of what you do. I see you as a very influential and intelligent man so I would love to hear your opinion about it. The topic talks about how having a skin tone or color preference is weird or basically racist. For me, I believe that it's not inherently racist but again, I would love to hear what you think. I'm sorry again if this is disturbing. Okay, let me try to be as politically correct as I can here. Look, having preferences in general is normal. A preference by itself isn't sexist, racist or classist. There are tons of guys who are into Asians or Latinas or some other girls. Is that bad? No, it's normal. Here's how a preference actually works. If a woman fits it, you cut her some slack on your other criteria. For example, I know a guy who is really into Asian women. With white, black or Latina girls, he is quite picky. But with Asian girls, honestly, her being Asian is already half the checklist done. Similar way, some guys can really be into black women, some into Slavic or white girls. It's not just ethnicity or skin color either. I know a guy who is obsessed with redheads. His standards drop the moment a redhead walks in. Some guys love blondes. Some love petite girls. Some love the strong fit, high-rex type athletic girls. Some like bigger boobs. Some like smaller. Some go for the model look. Some prefer curvier women. All of that is fine. Preferences are fine. Here's where it gets weird though. Say a guy tells me he prefers Slavic girls. Cool. But then I go, all right, what about Rihanna and Beyonce? Or Penelope Cruz and Salma Hayek in their prime? And he goes, eh, I'm not really into black or Latina girls. Now I've got questions. If you are saying you are not into objectively one of the prettiest women in the world, simply based on their race, then there might actually be something going on underneath. Because that's the difference. A real preference just means certain features pull you in stronger. It doesn't mean a woman outside that preference is automatically a no. So to answer the question directly, no. I don't think that having a skin tone or color preference is weird or racist. Refusing to acknowledge beauty in an entire group of women simply based on skin tone or color. That's where it starts to be questionable.
